subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing compaction-count-only late-success repair into an authoritative compaction completion reconciliation boundary, and which session fields should that boundary own?
rationale: The source gap is real, but deciding whether the boundary owns only durable accounting or also status snapshots, outcome metadata, auth-profile rotation, memory flush state, and recovery events is a product/architecture choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design the boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and ask the session-state owners to define the field ownership and monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

options.title: Limit to narrow bugs
options.body: Leave the current count-only repair in place and use focused follow-up issues or PRs for each stale status/activity field without creating a general completion event.

options.title: Declare current behavior sufficient
options.body: Close the broad follow-up if maintainers intentionally want only the count reconciliation and do not want a shared compaction completion boundary.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and ask the session-state owners to define the field ownership and monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent history on both the merged compaction reconciliation precursor and the session accessor/write seam likely to host this boundary.
